core_classification.analysis: Johannes privately avows that he still loves Victoria, strongly supporting T. The self-directed whisper, outstretched hands, and immediate repetition also give moderate independent support to E: the words function partly as an affective discharge when he is no longer speaking with her. Nothing indicates a commitment or relational undertaking, so P is unsupported.
core_classification.ambiguity: The E evidence is meaningful but not decisive: the episode can also be read as a highly emotional private avowal whose force remains predominantly truth-conditional.

utterance_status.description: A directly narrated but privately spoken utterance: after Victoria walks away, Johannes whispers “I still love you, love you” to himself rather than addressing it audibly to her.

contextual_interpretation: The declaration follows a guarded, wounded exchange in which Johannes and Victoria separate without openly acknowledging their attachment. Once she is walking away, Johannes contradicts his outward bitterness in a private avowal of continuing love. His reaching toward her and repeating the phrase suggest emotional overflow, but he does not use the declaration to undertake a commitment or alter their relationship; he calls only her name aloud afterward.

evidence.quotation_or_description: “jeg elsker Dem endnu, elsker Dem” (“I still love you, love you”).
evidence.supports: The present-tense declaration, especially “endnu” (‘still’), explicitly presents Johannes’s continuing love as true, strongly supporting T.

evidence.quotation_or_description: “Han strakte hænderne ut og hvisket, sa ømme ord for sig selv” (“He stretched out his hands and whispered, speaking tender words to himself”).
evidence.supports: The noncommunicative self-address and embodied reaching provide moderate evidence that producing the words partly serves as expressive affective discharge, supporting E independently of mere passionate delivery.

evidence.quotation_or_description: After the private declaration, he calls “Victoria!”; she turns but continues walking.
evidence.supports: Victoria does not receive the love declaration itself, and Johannes makes no promise or relational undertaking, weighing against P.

evidence.quotation_or_description: Immediately before parting, their dialogue is defensive and mutually wounded: “My impressions are as immaterial to you now as they were before.”
evidence.supports: The contrast between Johannes’s guarded public speech and subsequent private declaration frames the latter as a sincere-seeming avowal and emotional release.

ontology_assessment.diagnosis: T captures the explicit avowal of enduring love, while a moderate E score captures the self-directed expressive overflow. P is unnecessary, and no important aspect of the core force falls outside T/P/E.

notes: The analytical translation was used only to aid interpretation; quoted evidence is grounded in the supplied Norwegian source text.
